narrativeReportMd:
# Measure R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. The main issues are group-centric relocation of scoring/type/improvement metadata, removal or restructuring of topic/definition/guidance documentation fields, and R6 population/stratifier constructs that R4 cannot represent.

## Scope
Only Measure-local StructureDefinition changes are reported; inherited base-resource changes are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
Migrations need group-aware rules, documentation preservation rules, updated evaluator assumptions for optional criteria, and refreshed terminology dependencies.

## Highest-impact findings
The root-to-group move for scoring/type/compositeScoring/improvementNotation is the highest-impact hard break. The criteria relaxation/new alternatives are the highest R6-to-R4 and runtime risk.

## Follow-up analysis
Official diffs, rendered pages, ConceptMaps, and terminology expansions should be reviewed before production migration.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: Measure has material R4-to-R6 breaks: root interpretation metadata moved to groups, several documentation/categorization fields were removed or restructured, and R6 allows population/stratifier definitions that R4 cannot model.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Use group-aware transforms, preserve removed documentation deliberately, update evaluators for optional criteria and new alternatives, and refresh terminology caches/enums.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural deltas from the two StructureDefinitions. It is lower for terminology equivalence and rationale because external expansions and official diffs were unavailable.

findings.title: Measure-level scoring, type, compositeScoring, and improvementNotation moved under Measure.group

oldState.summary: R4 represented scoring, type, composite scoring, and improvement notation once at the Measure root; improvementNotation had a required R4 binding.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented scoring, type, composite scoring, and improvement notation once at the Measure root; improvementNotation had a required R4 binding.

newState.summary: R6 removes those root elements and adds optional group-level replacements; group.improvementNotation is extensible and uses a terminology.hl7.org value set.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes those root elements and adds optional group-level replacements; group.improvementNotation is extensible and uses a terminology.hl7.org value set.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances carrying these root fields are invalid in R6, and R6 group-specific values cannot be collapsed to one R4 root value without policy decisions. This is high risk because scoring, type, and improvement notation drive calculation interpretation and reporting.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow measure characteristics to vary by group.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the root scoring/type/compositeScoring/improvementNotation elements as deprecated measure-wide defaults while adding group-level fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of allowing scoring, type, composite scoring, and improvement notation to vary by group is reasonable because R6 groups can represent heterogeneous measure components. The breakage is substantial for R4 instances that used the root fields, but avoiding simultaneous root and group representations is a material design benefit. Without ballot rationale, the break cannot be called strictly necessary, but it is probably justified given the ambiguity a dual model would introduce.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have kept the R4 root elements as deprecated 0..1 or 0..* measure-wide defaults and added the new group-level elements. Converters could copy root values to each group, or R6 readers could treat root values as defaults when group values are absent. That would preserve most R4 instances while still allowing group-specific values. The tradeoff is a long-lived duplicate model with precedence questions when both root and group values are present or when groups intentionally differ.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common R4 Measures, but creates duplicate representations for measure characteristics, requires precedence rules, and risks indefinite support for root defaults.

evidence.detail: R4 contains the four root elements.
R6 contains the group-level replacements and lacks the root ids.

examples.examplesMd: Illustrative fragments focus on moved fields, not complete production Measures.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 instances carrying these root fields are invalid in R6, and R6 group-specific values cannot be collapsed to one R4 root value without policy decisions. This is high risk because scoring, type, and improvement notation drive calculation interpretation and reporting.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Strict R6 validation rejects the removed root properties. R6-to-R4 conversion is only safe when all groups share compatible values. Generated code and FHIRPath that read root paths will break.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move root values into each intended group. If groups differ, require manual review or preserve group-specific values in extensions when converting to R4.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The group-centric model is useful, but deprecated root defaults plus group overrides would have reduced instance breakage.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 measure-wide scoring, type, compositeScoring, and improvementNotation moved from the root to Measure.group in R6. This is a real old-valid/new-invalid and generated-path break, and the affected fields control measure interpretation rather than cosmetic metadata. However, the R6 goal is substantive: a single Measure can now express group-specific scoring/type/improvement semantics. Keeping root-level defaults as a compatibility alias would preserve simple R4 instances, but it would also create duplicate same-resource representations and precedence problems when group values intentionally differ.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot contains Measure.scoring, Measure.type, Measure.compositeScoring, and Measure.improvementNotation at the Measure root.
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot contains Measure.group.scoring, Measure.group.type, Measure.group.compositeScoring, and Measure.group.improvementNotation, with the root ids absent.

R4 Measure.improvementNotation has a required binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/measure-improvement-notation|4.0.1; R6 group.improvementNotation is extensibly bound to http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/measure-improvement-notation.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Measure is FMM 2 and trial-use, so FMM is neutral rather than a strong stability guarantee or a low-FMM softener. Because these fields are central to measure semantics, the compatibility mechanism and R6 design goal drove the judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with the root properties are not base R6 Measure instances. There is also runtime/API/codegen path churn and R6-to-R4 loss when group-specific values cannot be collapsed to one R4 root value.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have retained the root fields as deprecated measure-wide defaults while adding group-level overrides, preserving many R4 instances. The tradeoff is material: validators, renderers, and evaluators would need conflict and precedence rules whenever both root and group values are populated or groups diverge.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative assessment; I agree on the break mechanism, but view the group-specific design goal and duplicate-model tradeoff as enough to make the break probably OK.

findings.title: Measure.topic was removed without a direct R6 replacement

oldState.summary: R4 had Measure.topic 0..* CodeableConcept with an example definition-topic binding for repository categorization.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had Measure.topic 0..* CodeableConcept with an example definition-topic binding for repository categorization.

newState.summary: R6 Measure has no Measure.topic element in the base StructureDefinition.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 Measure has no Measure.topic element in the base StructureDefinition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 Measures with topic metadata contain an unknown element in R6. The likely impact is catalog/search behavior rather than calculation.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep Measure.topic as deprecated optional categorization metadata while steering new R6 content to useContext or catalog metadata.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Consolidating categorization metadata is a reasonable goal, but removing `Measure.topic` creates a direct validation break for R4 catalog/search metadata. The local evidence does not show that invalidating that optional field was necessary to achieve the R6 goal. Living with the older topic field as deprecated metadata would have preserved R4 instances with modest long-term cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `Measure.topic` 0..* CodeableConcept as a deprecated legacy categorization field, clarified that `useContext` or other catalog metadata is preferred for new content, and optionally specified how topic values should feed search facets. This would preserve R4-valid topic-bearing Measures while still encouraging consolidation. The cost is carrying one legacy category surface and possible overlap in repository search implementations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Low to moderate: an overlapping categorization path remains, but it is optional metadata and does not conflict with measure calculation semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 Measures with topic metadata contain an unknown element in R6. The likely impact is catalog/search behavior rather than calculation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 topic-bearing instances are old-valid/new-invalid. There is no R6 base element to back-port.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map topics by local policy, likely to useContext, catalog metadata, or an extension; update search facets accordingly.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping topic deprecated or publishing an official mapping would have avoided data loss.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Measure.topic was optional categorization metadata used for searching, sorting, and filtering. An R4 Measure carrying topic becomes invalid against the R6 base resource, and R6 does not add a direct replacement; useContext already existed in R4 and is not a lossless path-level continuation. The field is not part of measure calculation, but keeping an optional deprecated topic element would have been a low-cost way to preserve old catalog metadata while steering new content elsewhere.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot has Measure.topic 0..* CodeableConcept with an example definition-topic binding.
R6 local Measure paths list no Measure.topic element.
R6 still has Measure.useContext, but that path was already present in R4 and is not a direct structural replacement for topic.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Measure is FMM 2 and trial-use, which is neutral. It does not by itself require preserving every optional metadata field, but it also does not excuse a direct validation break where a modest deprecated-field alternative exists.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 topic-bearing instances contain an unknown base element in R6. The practical downstream effect is catalog/search metadata loss rather than calculation failure.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. Retaining Measure.topic as deprecated 0..* CodeableConcept while documenting a preferred R6 categorization approach would preserve R4 instances. The main cost is a small overlapping metadata surface, not a difficult semantic conflict.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Medium impact and Yes less-breaking alternative judgment.

findings.title: Measure.definition markdown list was replaced by structured Measure.term

oldState.summary: R4 Measure.definition was 0..* markdown for defined terms used in measure documentation.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 Measure.definition was 0..* markdown for defined terms used in measure documentation.

newState.summary: R6 removes Measure.definition and adds Measure.term 0..* BackboneElement with optional code and definition children.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes Measure.definition and adds Measure.term 0..* BackboneElement with optional code and definition children.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 definition arrays are invalid in R6. R6 term.code has no R4 native slot, so reverse conversion can lose coded term identity.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent defined terms with optional coded identity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain Measure.definition as deprecated legacy markdown while adding Measure.term for coded or structured term definitions.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding `Measure.term` is a reasonable way to support coded term identity and a clearer term-definition structure. The evidence does not show that the old markdown list had to be made invalid, especially because old definitions could be interpreted as uncoded terms. However, retaining both `definition` and `term.definition` would create a real duplicate-representation problem, so the less-breaking alternative is only partial rather than clearly superior.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `Measure.definition` 0..* markdown and add `Measure.term`; old `definition` entries would remain valid and could be treated as uncoded term definitions. New R6 content needing coded identity would use `term.code` and `term.definition`. The downside is validation and rendering ambiguity when both fields describe the same term, plus long-lived support for two same-resource shapes.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 documentation, but creates two native places for uncoded term definitions and requires deduplication or precedence guidance.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 definition arrays are invalid in R6. R6 term.code has no R4 native slot, so reverse conversion can lose coded term identity.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with definition are old-valid/new-invalid. R6 term.definition can be flattened to R4 text, but term.code needs an extension or is lost.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap each R4 definition string as term.definition; populate term.code only when local conventions support it. Preserve R6 term.code by extension when back-porting.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding term while keeping definition deprecated would have been less disruptive but would create duplicate representations.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 Measure.definition was a repeatable markdown string, while R6 replaces it with a repeatable Measure.term backbone that can carry both a coded term and a markdown definition. Old R4 definition arrays are invalid in R6, but forward migration is usually mechanical by wrapping each string as term.definition. The new term.code field adds capability that R4 did not have. Retaining both definition and term would reduce migration friction, but would create two native places for the same uncoded term definitions.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot has Measure.definition 0..* markdown.
R6 local Measure paths omit Measure.definition and add Measure.term 0..*, Measure.term.code 0..1 CodeableConcept, and Measure.term.definition 0..1 markdown.
R6 Measure.term.code has an example binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/measure-definition-example.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Measure is FMM 2 trial-use, so the maturity signal is neutral. The judgment turns on the narrow documentation-path break and whether the structured term model justifies it.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 definition arrays do not validate as R6. There is also R6-to-R4 loss if term.code is populated because R4 has no native coded term slot.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have kept Measure.definition as deprecated while adding Measure.term. That would preserve old instances, but it would also require rendering, validation, and conversion rules for duplicate uncoded definitions when both fields are present.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative assessment; I agree on the mechanism but judge the structured term model's tradeoffs as proportionate.

findings.title: Measure.guidance was removed; migration to usage is plausible but lossy

oldState.summary: R4 had separate Measure.usage 0..1 string and Measure.guidance 0..1 markdown.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had separate Measure.usage 0..1 string and Measure.guidance 0..1 markdown.

newState.summary: R6 has no guidance element; usage remains 0..1 but is markdown and comments that this metadata was typically called Guidance in HQMF.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 has no guidance element; usage remains 0..1 but is markdown and comments that this metadata was typically called Guidance in HQMF.

facts.newValue: Medium; inferred from R6 usage comment, not a local ConceptMap

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with guidance are invalid in R6. If R4 usage and guidance are both populated, R6 has only one native usage slot, so a converter must merge, prioritize, or use an extension.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep Measure.guidance as deprecated optional markdown while making Measure.usage markdown and documenting the preferred consolidation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Consolidating guidance-like documentation into `usage` is reasonable, and changing `usage` to markdown supports richer text. But invalidating `Measure.guidance` appears avoidable because it is optional documentation and does not structurally conflict with the R6 `usage` field. A deprecated legacy field would have preserved all R4 guidance content while allowing new R6 authors to use the consolidated location.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `Measure.guidance` 0..1 markdown as deprecated and clarified that new guidance should be placed in `usage`, or that both fields should be rendered under distinct headings when both are present. That would preserve R4 instances and still advance consolidation. The main cost is carrying an overlapping documentation field and specifying a merge/display policy.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Legacy overlap between usage and guidance persists; converters and renderers need display or merge guidance when both fields are present.

evidence.detail: R6 usage is markdown and references Guidance in HQMF.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 instances with guidance are invalid in R6. If R4 usage and guidance are both populated, R6 has only one native usage slot, so a converter must merge, prioritize, or use an extension.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R6 rejects the removed guidance element. R6 usage can be carried as text in R4, but the old distinction between clinical usage and detailed guidance may be lost.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a policy to concatenate with headings, preserve guidance in an extension, or require author review when both fields are present.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping guidance deprecated would have allowed old content to validate while authors consolidated documentation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 had both usage and guidance, while R6 removes guidance and changes usage to markdown with a comment that this metadata was typically called Guidance in HQMF. An R4 instance with guidance is invalid in R6, and if both R4 usage and guidance are populated, a converter must merge, label, or extend to avoid losing the distinction. This is documentation, not executable criteria, but guidance can affect safe and correct measure implementation. A deprecated guidance field would have preserved R4 content with modest cost.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot has Measure.usage 0..1 string and Measure.guidance 0..1 markdown.
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot has Measure.usage 0..1 markdown and no Measure.guidance element.
R6 Measure.usage comment says the metadata element was typically referred to as Guidance in HQMF.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Measure is FMM 2 trial-use, so FMM is neutral. The documentation nature softens the severity, but not enough to dismiss a lossy merge where a simple deprecated-field alternative exists.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 guidance is not an R6 base element. The direct downstream risk is semantic/documentation loss when guidance and usage must be collapsed into one R6 usage field.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could have retained Measure.guidance as deprecated optional markdown while recommending Measure.usage for new content. The tradeoff is an overlapping documentation field and the need to define display behavior when both usage and guidance are present.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing Medium impact and Yes less-breaking alternative judgment.

findings.title: Population and value-based stratifier criteria are no longer mandatory in R6

oldState.summary: R4 required group.population.criteria and group.stratifier.component.criteria as 1..1 Expression. group.stratifier.criteria was already optional, and supplementalData.criteria remains required in R6.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required group.population.criteria and group.stratifier.component.criteria as 1..1 Expression. group.stratifier.criteria was already optional, and supplementalData.criteria remains required in R6.

newState.summary: R6 lowers population.criteria and stratifier.component.criteria to 0..1 and adds groupDefinition, valueSet, unit, basis, and basisRequirement alternatives.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 lowers population.criteria and stratifier.component.criteria to 0..1 and adds groupDefinition, valueSet, unit, basis, and basisRequirement alternatives.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break, but valid R6 Measures may omit criteria that R4 validators, generated APIs, and evaluators assumed were mandatory.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R6 relaxes R4 required criteria and adds optional alternatives, so R4 criteria-containing instances are not made invalid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting definitional groups, value-set stratifiers, and non-subject or population-basis measures is a reasonable R6 goal. Because the R4-to-R6 direction is permissive rather than breaking, the reported impact is mainly runtime handling and R6-to-R4 representability. Keeping R4 criteria mandatory would be less expressive and could force artificial expressions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: There is no applicable backward-compatible alternative for preserving R4 instances because the R6 design already preserves R4 Measures that contain the required criteria. The compatibility work is in downgrade policy: R6 Measures that use only `groupDefinition`, `valueSet`, `basis`, or `basisRequirement` cannot always be represented in R4 without synthesis or extensions, but that is not an R4-to-R6 base-design break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base design is needed; the tradeoff is evaluator updates and R6-to-R4 conversion policy for criteria-free or groupDefinition/valueSet-based content.

findings.narrativeMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break, but valid R6 Measures may omit criteria that R4 validators, generated APIs, and evaluators assumed were mandatory.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is relaxed. R6-to-R4 fails when no Expression can be synthesized for the required R4 criteria fields. Runtime code must handle absent criteria.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update evaluators for optional criteria and new R6 alternatives. Reject or manually review R6-to-R4 conversions that use group definitions or value-based stratifiers without expressions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: R6 expressiveness appears justified; preserving R4 criteria requiredness would force artificial expressions.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Lowering population.criteria and stratifier.component.criteria from required to optional does not break R4-to-R6 validation: R4 instances that have criteria still fit the R6 cardinality. The burden is on upgraded evaluators, generated APIs, and R6-to-R4 converters that can no longer assume an Expression exists. Because the R6 model adds groupDefinition, valueSet, basis, and basisRequirement patterns for non-subject and definitional-group measures, keeping R4-required expressions would force artificial expressions or block the new modeling goal.
keyEvidence: R4 Measure.group.population.criteria is 1..1 Expression; R6 lowers it to 0..1 Expression.
R4 Measure.group.stratifier.component.criteria is 1..1 Expression; R6 lowers it to 0..1 Expression.
R6 adds Measure.group.population.groupDefinition, Measure.group.stratifier.groupDefinition, Measure.group.stratifier.component.valueSet, Measure.group.basis, and Measure.group.basisRequirement.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Measure is FMM 2 trial-use, so FMM is neutral. The affected criteria are central to evaluation, which keeps the runtime concern real, but the change is widening for R4-to-R6 instances.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: R6 consumers must handle absent criteria where R4 models could require it. R6-to-R4 loss also occurs when a valid R6 Measure uses groupDefinition or valueSet without an Expression that can be synthesized for R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No clear less-breaking base design. Keeping criteria mandatory would preserve old assumptions but would undermine the R6 alternatives or require dummy expressions. An invariant requiring at least one definition mechanism might improve R6 authoring quality, but it is not a less-breaking design for preserving R4-valid instances.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High runtime/R6-to-R4 impact and Not applicable alternative assessment, with the caveat that this is not an R4-to-R6 instance validation break.

findings.title: Several local string fields changed to markdown primitives

affectedLocation.oldPath: Measure.usage / Measure.rateAggregation / Measure.riskAdjustment / group and supplementalData description fields
affectedLocation.oldElementId: Measure.usage / Measure.rateAggregation / Measure.riskAdjustment / group and supplementalData description fields

oldState.summary: R4 used string for usage, rateAggregation, riskAdjustment, group.description, population.description, stratifier.description, stratifier.component.description, and supplementalData.description.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used string for usage, rateAggregation, riskAdjustment, group.description, population.description, stratifier.description, stratifier.component.description, and supplementalData.description.

newState.summary: R6 uses markdown for those same paths. JSON still carries primitive values as strings.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses markdown for those same paths. JSON still carries primitive values as strings.

facts.note: usage, rateAggregation, riskAdjustment, group.description, population.description, stratifier.description, stratifier.component.description, supplementalData.description

impact.impactRationaleMd: Plain R4 string values should remain JSON-compatible, but generated classes, schemas, FHIRPath type checks, and renderers may change. R6 markdown formatting can be lost in R4 systems that expect plain strings.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer formatting for human-readable Measure text.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the affected elements typed as string and clarify in definitions that markdown syntax may be used and rendered.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of allowing richer formatted Measure text is reasonable. Existing R4 primitive string values remain largely wire-compatible because markdown is serialized as a JSON string, so this is not a normal old-valid/new-invalid instance break. The remaining breakage is generated-type, schema, FHIRPath, and rendering behavior. A less-breaking convention-only design exists, but it would not give base R6 tooling a reliable markdown type, so the primitive type change is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained the affected elements as `string` and updated their definitions or comments to say markdown formatting is allowed or expected. That would reduce code-generation churn and preserve older API assumptions. It only partially meets the R6 goal because generic tooling would not be able to infer from the base type that markdown rendering and sanitization are required.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves generated string APIs, but weakens the computable signal that these fields require markdown-aware rendering and sanitization.

r6NotRepresentableInR4Json.riskAdjustment:
**Risk adjustment:** use model coefficients.

See Appendix A.

findings.narrativeMd: Plain R4 string values should remain JSON-compatible, but generated classes, schemas, FHIRPath type checks, and renderers may change. R6 markdown formatting can be lost in R4 systems that expect plain strings.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Not normally old-valid/new-invalid at the JSON value level. Risk appears in codegen/runtime and in R6-to-R4 display fidelity.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate models and update renderers/forms for markdown. Test plain text and multi-paragraph markdown.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping string would preserve generated APIs but hide markdown rendering expectations.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The affected fields changed from string to markdown, but both primitives are serialized as JSON strings and the fields are human-readable descriptions rather than structural calculation inputs. Existing plain string content should remain wire-compatible in ordinary R6 instances. Implementers may need to regenerate models or make renderers markdown-aware, but that is a limited tooling/runtime update, not a material base compatibility problem.
keyEvidence: R4 Measure.usage, Measure.rateAggregation, Measure.riskAdjustment, group.description, population.description, stratifier.description, stratifier.component.description, and supplementalData.description use type string.
R6 uses type markdown at the same retained paths.
The local snapshots show unchanged cardinalities for the retained description paths.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Measure is FMM 2 trial-use, so FMM is neutral. The wire-compatible primitive shape and documentation-only nature dominate the judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: some generated models and renderers distinguish markdown from string, but there is no normal old-valid/new-invalid JSON instance break for plain text values.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial but unnecessary. R6 could have kept string and allowed markdown by prose convention, reducing codegen churn. That would lose the computable signal that these fields need markdown-aware display and sanitization; given the wire compatibility, the base design does not need renewed attention.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing no-hard-break and Partial alternative assessment, but disagree with treating this as Medium impact.

findings.title: Measure.subject[x] binding changed and group-level subject scoping was added

oldState.summary: R4 subject[x] was CodeableConcept or Reference(Group), extensibly bound to subject-type using resource-types codes.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 subject[x] was CodeableConcept or Reference(Group), extensibly bound to subject-type using resource-types codes.

newState.summary: R6 root subject[x] is extensibly bound to participant-resource-types using fhir-types codes, and R6 adds group.subject[x].
newState.narrativeMd: R6 root subject[x] is extensibly bound to participant-resource-types using fhir-types codes, and R6 adds group.subject[x].

impact.impactRationaleMd: The binding remains extensible, so this is not normally a hard base validation error. Terminology-aware profiles may flag legacy codings, and group-specific subject context has no R4 native representation.

justification.inferredGoal: Broaden and scope subject context by group.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Define the R6 subject value set to include the old resource-types codings during transition while adding fhir-types participant codings and group.subject.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Broadening subject context and allowing group-level subject scoping are reasonable R6 goals. The base element shape remains compatible and the binding is extensible, so this is not usually a hard validation break. A less-breaking terminology design could have accepted the old `resource-types` codings as well, but that would make Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, and Device representable through parallel systems for an indefinite period.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base-design alternative is not ordinary conversion guidance or a ConceptMap alone; it would be an R6 value set that explicitly includes both the old `http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-types` codings and the new `http://hl7.org/fhir/fhir-types` participant codings, while still adding `Measure.group.subject[x]`. This would reduce terminology churn for R4 instances. The tradeoff is persistent coding duplication and ambiguity for search, validation, and normalization.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces terminology warnings for old codings, but prolongs duplicate code systems for the same subject concepts and complicates terminology normalization.

evidence.detail: R4 includes Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, Device from resource-types.
R6 includes broader participant types from fhir-types.

findings.narrativeMd: The binding remains extensible, so this is not normally a hard base validation error. Terminology-aware profiles may flag legacy codings, and group-specific subject context has no R4 native representation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old CodeableConcepts may produce terminology warnings rather than errors. R6 group subjects must be collapsed, dropped, or extended for R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map resource-types codings to fhir-types codings. Convert group subjects to R4 only when all groups share the same subject; otherwise require review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Including legacy codings or an official ConceptMap would reduce migration ambiguity.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The root subject[x] element keeps the same broad shape, but its extensible binding changes from subject-type/resource-types to participant-resource-types/fhir-types, and R6 adds group.subject[x]. Old root subject codings may trigger terminology normalization work rather than a structural base validation failure. The real compatibility issue is reverse and semantic: group-specific subject context can be central to evaluation and cannot always be represented in R4. The broader participant list and group scoping are coherent R6 goals, and a compatibility value set containing both code systems would create long-lived duplicate codings for the same subject concepts.
keyEvidence: R4 Measure.subject[x] is CodeableConcept or Reference with an extensible binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/subject-type.
R4 ValueSet-subject-type includes Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, and Device from http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-types.

R6 ValueSet-participant-resource-types includes broader fhir-types concepts such as CareTeam, Group, PractitionerRole, and RelatedPerson.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Measure is FMM 2 trial-use, so FMM is neutral. Subject context is important to evaluation, so the reverse/semantic risk remains meaningful despite the extensible binding.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: group.subject[x] has no R4 native location unless all group subjects can be collapsed to root subject[x]. The root binding change is mostly warning-level terminology pressure rather than an old-valid/new-invalid structural break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have included the old resource-types codings in the participant value set while adding fhir-types and group.subject[x]. That would reduce terminology churn for R4 instances but would institutionalize parallel code systems and complicate search, validation, and normalization.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative assessment; I put less weight on hard R4-to-R6 validation risk and more on R6-to-R4 loss for group-specific subjects.

justification.justificationRationaleMd: Centralizing reusable terminology and adding example bindings for new R6 concepts are reasonable goals. The local inputs do not show that changing established binding canonical URLs was necessary to meet those goals, especially where the affected Measure bindings are not hard instance constraints. Stable binding URLs would have reduced terminology-service and generated-enum churn while still allowing the value sets to be published from a terminology package.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 base design could have continued to bind retained Measure elements to their R4 value set URLs, such as `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/measure-population` and `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/measure-data-usage`, while publishing or maintaining those value sets through terminology.hl7.org infrastructure. This is different from a ConceptMap or migration note: the base binding URL itself would remain stable. The tradeoff is alias management and less uniform terminology.hl7.org naming, not a fundamental failure of the terminology-governance goal.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves cached terminology and generated binding metadata with low to moderate alias-management cost, but reduces uniformity of terminology.hl7.org canonical URLs.
